chapter: Goodman, Woody Herman and the Army
title: Joining Benny Goodman through Ben Webster
summary: Ben Webster and Jimmy Maxwell got him the Goodman job after Mel Powell left; Goodman's sciatica and ray made him hard to work with.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: So then I got my chance. One of the waitresses said that a guy wanted to talk me. And it was Benny's brother; and Benny wanted me. Then Jimmy Maxwell, the first trumpet player with Benny Goodman... Benny and Mel Powell had had a fight, and they were through. So Jimmy Maxwell was a good friend of Ben Webster's, and he talked to him about it, and he got me the job -- Ben told him to get me.

Because they were coming to California to make a picture anyway. So they sent ahead and they got me. And I stayed with him about...oh, four or five months. He was suffering from sciatica, which I knew nothing about. No wonder he was hard to get along with. And he was constantly using that ray, you know, and whenever he would find anybody

that he could get away with on it... And he used it on me, and I got mad. I didn't like it. And I didn't... I had gone on the wagon, because I wanted to play good for him. But I decided to go with the guys finally at intermission and started going across the street, and then I'd come back and then I'd put him on, play and all that... I almost had a fist-fight with him one night, begged him to fire me...
